The test image shows a mango leaf with several discrete, dark brown-to-black lesions scattered across the leaf surface. The lesions are irregular/rounded, sunken-looking, and well-defined against the otherwise green leaf. This pattern is characteristic of Anthracnose (dark necrotic spots).

Now let me view one reference image from Anthracnose to confirm:

The Anthracnose reference shows a more advanced/yellowed stage. However, key observations from the test image:

- **Discrete, dark brown-black necrotic lesions** scattered on an otherwise green leaf
- Lesions are irregular, slightly sunken-looking
- No white/gray powder (rules out Powdery_Mildew)
- No sooty coating over broad areas (rules out Sooty_Mould)
- No tip/stem dieback (rules out Die_Back)

These discrete dark spots on a green mango leaf are the hallmark of Anthracnose infection.
